_meta.description: Operational readiness targets for the six-person advance crew plus 100 arriving civilians. Delivered emergency systems and uncommissioned prefab cargo receive no credit.
references: NASA-STD-3001 — Human spaceflight crew health standards
NASA ECLSS — Environmental Control and Life Support System specifications
NASA MOXIE — Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment
Drysdale et al. 2003 — Advanced life support sizing analysis

oxygen_production.description: A conjunctive oxygen contract: commissioned, powered and water-fed generation plus separate settlement tankage for a thirty-day 106-person reserve. The precursor lander tank receives no readiness credit.
oxygen_production.scientific_basis: NASA OCHMO ECLSS sizing gives 1.083 kg O2/person/day including exercise. 106 occupants require 114.798 kg/day, rounded upward to 114.8 kg/day.

water_supply.description: A conjunctive water contract: new water extraction replaces loop losses, separate wastewater hardware treats the gross hygiene and metabolic stream, and modular settlement tanks hold thirty days of configured external make-up. Purification never counts as extraction and the precursor lander tank earns no readiness credit.
water_supply.scientific_basis: External make-up covers 318 L/day for 106 occupants plus 2,400 L/day crop-loop loss after 90% recovery across six 1,000 m2 farms. Separate wastewater hardware treats the 2,650 L/day crew hygiene and metabolic stream.

food_production.description: Mature, powered controlled-environment agriculture sized for the full diet of 106 occupants; a newly commissioned but unharvested farm receives no capacity credit.
food_production.scientific_basis: The same 2,700 kcal/person/day planning allowance used for the active advance crew is retained for the operational settlement contract.

shelter_capacity.description: Pressurized, thermally regulated, radiation-shielded living space. Each module provides life support for a set number of occupants.
shelter_capacity.scientific_basis: NASA habitat concepts suggest ~8-12m² per person for extended habitation. Regolith-shielded modules provide radiation protection (2-3m regolith ≈ Earth-equivalent shielding).

energy_infrastructure.description: Solar panel arrays, battery storage, and power distribution for all colony systems. Must cover O2 production, water processing, heating/cooling, lighting, and equipment.
energy_infrastructure.scientific_basis: Six 1,000 m2 controlled farms draw 15.6 MW at the configured NASA BVAD lighting allocation. The 18 MW firm-service target adds habitat, ECLSS, water, communications and operating margin; solar recipe credit is derated below physical peak and includes finite storage.

hazard_protection.description: The storm-safe section integrated into every commissioned, regolith-shielded habitat protects that habitat's twelve occupants from acute radiation events.
hazard_protection.scientific_basis: Water and hydrogen-rich polymer lining plus local regolith overburden provide the required mass shielding. Integrating the refuge into each pressure habitat avoids a duplicate pressure hull and still requires physical installation and radiation acceptance before either score is awarded.

score_calculation.notes: Each sub-target is capped at 1.0 (building excess O2 doesn't compensate for missing water). The overall score represents balanced readiness across all systems.
